## 2026-11-21 · 163 · FERB knows its contained processes by its own record, and never asks another program's sandbox

**The bug (journal 161).** ferb-shell's `listeners::contained` decided whether a process holding a local port was
inside FERB's containment by asking the kernel about that process's sandbox: `sandbox_check(pid, "file-read-data",
~/.ferb/run)` must say denied and the same for the workspace allowed. Two faults, both in Python's `listeners.py:44`
too (git 9d3f84bc, `ferb/act/shell/listeners.py`), so this is fixed against Python:
- Another program's sandbox can answer the same way (the test guard's offline.sb did), and its servers then got
  the trust FERB gives its own commands' servers.
- Asking runs the asked process's own sandbox actions as if it had tried: FERB killed guarded test binaries, and
  could end any sandboxed program on the Mac that acts on those paths.

**What the check is for.** Three places trust a contained process. The profile lets a command connect directly to
the ports whose every listener was contained when it started (HAND-214, `sandbox.rs` `network`). FERB's proxy lets
a command reach an unpinned local port only when the socket that holds the connection is contained (`local.rs`
`LocalAccess::verified`, HAND-226/227/433). The stop of a group whose first process has ended signals it only when
every member is contained (`manager.rs` `ours`, `pty.rs` `kill`: the group id could be reused by another program).

**The fix (HAND-650).** A process is contained when it is a shell command FERB started under its profile, or a
descendant of one, by facts the kernel sets and no other program can claim:
- `pty.rs` `spawn`: for an argv under `sandbox-exec` (not an admin command: sudo runs outside the profile), the
  child reads its own kernel unique id between fork and exec and writes it to a pipe that closes at exec. Spawn
  returns after the exec, so the id is already there; FERB reads it without waiting, so a command that ends at once
  is still recorded. Exactly one 8-byte write counts, which covers another thread's child holding a copy of the
  pipe from the moment before its close-on-exec flag was set. A child that can still be read must have that id.
  `listeners::launched` records it.
- `listeners.rs` `contained`: reads the process's `proc_pidinfo` PROC_PIDT_BSDINFOWITHUNIQID record (its unique id,
  the unique id of the process that forked it, its parent's pid now). It is contained if either id is in FERB's
  record. If not, the walk goes to the living parent, which must still be the process that forked it (same unique
  id, so a reused pid never matches) and ends at launchd or anything unreadable. Every process found ours is
  remembered for the daemon's life, so a child stays contained after its parent ends. Unique ids are never reused
  while the Mac is up. The record is kept in the process (one per daemon), not passed around.
- The watch (`listeners.rs` `watch`, `sweep`): from the first recorded command, while any recorded command runs,
  every WATCH_S (HAND-232's second) FERB lists every process on the Mac. In order of unique id (parents before
  children), it records each process whose forking parent is already known. The same sweep runs at each listener
  scan (`local_listeners_now`) and when a recorded command's own process ends (`pty.rs` `run`, before its tree is
  gone). A server that detaches from its command through a helper that lived at least one tick (pg_ctl waits for
  postgres to start) is then recorded before the helper ends, and stays contained. The thread stops when no recorded
  command is left in a full listing, and the next recorded command starts it again.
- One path for every caller: `local_listeners_now`, `MacFacts::contained` (the proxy) and `ManagerConfig::new`'s
  `contained` all call it. `SocketFacts::contained`, `local_listeners_now` and `outside_ports` no longer take FERB's
  home and workspace. Nothing in the engine calls `sandbox_check` now (the two tests below keep a copy of the old
  question to show what it did).

**Named differences from Python (deliberate; all fail closed).**
- A server whose forking parent ended before FERB saw that parent is outside, though it still runs in FERB's
  sandbox: reached neither directly nor through the proxy. FERB sees the parent within one tick of the watch or at
  any check, so what remains outside is a detach that completes in less than about a second. Example: the subshell
  of `(cmd &)`, which ends at once. Measured with a helper that forks `nc` and ends after the given time, checked
  1.7 s later (6 tries each): 0 s (`(cmd &)`) 0/6 contained, 0.2 s 0/6, 0.5 s 4/6, 0.8 s 6/6, 1.2 s 6/6.
  pg_ctl's helper lives until postgres is ready. Python's docstring named pg_ctl as reachable; a pg_ctl that ends
  in under a second may now be outside. A plain `cmd &` stays contained after its command ends, because the kernel
  still names the command as its forking parent.
- After the daemon restarts, commands left running by the earlier daemon are outside.
- mac.applescript's and publish's sandboxed processes are no longer counted as contained. They hold no listeners
  that FERB's commands use.
- An admin command's processes are not recorded. They run as root, so their sockets were already outside (pid
  None) and FERB can't signal them.

**Kept.** offline.sb's carve-out (TEST-514) stays: FERB.app builds installed before this one still ask the old
question. `ferbs_containment_question_never_ends_a_guarded_binary` now asks that old question itself and checks
today's `contained`.

**Ruled out (in HAND-650's `rejected`).**
- An audit session per command: `setaudit_addr` with AU_ASSIGN_ASID gave EPERM unprivileged.
- Process group or session ids: setsid leaves them, and an emptied group's id can be reused.
- A disclaimed spawn's responsible process: a private API that changes whose TCC grants a command runs under.

**Tests (temporary folders only; only processes the tests start are signalled).**
- `tests/live.rs` `a_foreign_sandbox_that_answers_like_ferbs_is_outside_and_never_disturbed`: two `nc` listeners
  under foreign profiles that deny the test home's `.ferb/run` (one with `(with send-signal SIGKILL)`). Their ports
  are outside, `contained` is false and neither is signalled. Then Python's question, asked by the test, calls the
  plain one FERB's and kills the other (SIGKILL), which shows both are real cases of the bug.
- `ferbs_own_command_and_its_child_are_contained_and_stay_so_after_it_ends`: a command started through
  ShellManager backgrounds `nc`. The command and its child are contained and the port is inside, during the command
  and after it exits. The task's stop then ends the child (`ours`). The same holds for a command that ends at once
  after backgrounding its child. Passed 3 runs in a row.
- `a_server_detached_through_a_helper_that_lived_a_second_stays_contained`: the pg_ctl shape. A helper forks `nc`,
  lives 1.5 s and ends, and nothing asks about the server meanwhile. Afterwards the server's parent is launchd, it
  is contained, its port is inside, and the task's stop ends it. With the watch disabled the test fails at
  `contained`.
- `listeners.rs` unit test `a_sweep_records_a_living_tree_in_one_pass_and_says_whether_a_command_runs`: a
  grandchild listed before its parent, a foreign process, ended commands, and a command recorded after the listing.
- `listeners.rs` unit test `descent_is_followed_by_unique_ids_and_a_reused_pid_never_matches`: scripted lineages
  cover a grandchild through a living parent, a reused parent pid, unreadable and unknown processes, memory after the
  parent ends, a backgrounded child of the command, and an orphan of an unseen parent.
- The whole ferb-shell suite passes through ferb-test-guard as the gate runs it, and so does ferb-test-guard's. fmt
  is clean, and clippy -D warnings is clean for ferb-shell and ferb-test-guard.

**Unverified.**
- The whole workspace's checks; ferbd builds the proxy with `LocalAccess::new`, whose signature is unchanged.
- The watch's cost was measured only on this Mac, in a debug build. With 750 processes a sweep takes 0.47 ms of CPU
  (0.49 ms wall), about 0.05% of one core per second while a recorded command runs, and nothing otherwise. A full
  listener scan with its sweep took 18.4 ms, mostly reading the sockets as before. Not measured on the owner's
  Mac or in a release build.
- PROC_PIDT_BSDINFOWITHUNIQID is in xnu's headers but not the public SDK. The record size (192 bytes) was checked
  on this Mac (macOS 27.2). Any other size is treated as unreadable, so a change fails closed.
- A live check on the owner's installed FERB.app: a dev server a task starts is still reached through the proxy and
  directly.

## 2026-11-22 · 164 · The phone's lock screen follows the screenshot switch; FERB's service comes back after any stop not its own

**Lock screen (PHN-793 owner, PHN-794 ruling, superseding PHN-505).** Android's MainActivity set FLAG_SECURE on
`block || mustSecure || locked`, so the lock page was black in screenshots whatever the owner's switch said. The rule
is now `ScreenGuard.secure(block, mustSecure)` (apps/android/.../ScreenGuard.kt), applied to the window the same way:
FLAG_SECURE still goes on before the first frame, Watch live, a task's short view, the Mac's camera and a hidden
answer's box (the view model's mustSecure) still force it, and `setRecentsScreenshotEnabled(false)` (PHN-15) is
unchanged. Checked before changing: the lock page (design Pages.kt UnlockPage) takes no data, only FERB's mark,
"FERB is locked", a fixed line and the unlock button; sheets and the first-run asks are drawn only for the PAIR and
MAIN gates (ui/Root.kt); the unlock is BiometricPrompt with BIOMETRIC_STRONG | DEVICE_CREDENTIAL, so the PIN is
typed in the system's own window. iPhone had no such rule: PrivacyCover (FerbAppUI Privacy.swift) takes the switch
and mustSecure only and nothing on iOS blocks a screenshot of the lock page; a test now pins that the locked model is
not a private screen. PHN-505's test citations moved to PHN-794.

**Background service (DMN-618 owner, DMN-619 ruling).** The owner: a stopped service must come back by itself. Today
launchd (KeepAlive {SuccessfulExit false}) restarted a crash, but the daemon exited 0 on every SIGTERM, so a `kill`,
Activity Monitor's Quit or macOS's Quit & Reopen left it stopped. KeepAlive true was looked at and not taken: it
restarts FERB's own stops too (Installer::stop's `launchctl kill SIGTERM` before the store clean-up's work would see
a fresh daemon start beside the work; `update.prepare`'s stop would bring the old daemon back while Sparkle replaces
the app and the app's exit wait would see its socket again; a newer store would start and exit every 5 s), and a
hold for it would need a path the fixed in-app definition can't name. Instead the definition stays as it is and the
daemon picks its exit code (ferbd run.rs): 0 for `update.prepare`, for a newer store, and for a signal while
`~/.ferb/service.stopping` names its pid; 128 + the signal for any other SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP, after the same
clean shutdown. ferb-device `Installer::stop` writes the marker (atomically, the pid it read from `launchctl print`)
before its SIGTERM and clears it if its wait fails; `Installer::start` (resume_service) clears it whatever happened.
A daemon that has started drops a marker naming another pid and keeps one naming itself (FERB's stop can come while it
is still starting). Upgrade: the definition is byte-for-byte the same apart from its comment, and an older daemon
stopped by a newer `ferb` still exits 0 on SIGTERM, so it stays stopped for the work as before. A checkout's
LaunchAgent (install.rs `plist`, same KeepAlive) gets the same behavior; its unload is a bootout, never restarted.
FERB.app's Quit never stopped the daemon (Application.swift `applicationWillTerminate` tears down the app only) and
still doesn't, so there is no Quit path to exempt.

Probe of launchd's behavior on this Mac (macOS 27.2), with a disposable LaunchAgent `com.example.keepaliveprobe`
(KeepAlive {SuccessfulExit false}, ThrottleInterval 2, booted out after): exit 143 after an unasked SIGTERM was
restarted, SIGKILL was restarted, exit 0 after a marked SIGTERM stayed stopped (`last exit code = 0`) until
kickstart, bootout restarted nothing.

**Named differences from Python.** main.py exited 0 on every signal; the Rust daemon exits 128 + the signal unless
the stop is FERB's own (DMN-619). The installer fixture's commands are unchanged (the marker is a file written and
removed inside one step, so no step's file changes differ).

**Tests.** Android `ScreenGuardTest` (Robolectric, the window's FLAG_SECURE for the four cases); iOS
`AppModelTests.testTheLockPageFollowsTheScreenshotSwitch` (all 26 AppModelTests pass on the simulator). ferbd
`lifecycle.rs only_ferbs_own_stop_keeps_the_service_stopped` (143, the log line, `daemon.stopped` journaled, a
stale marker dropped); `services.rs a_hang_up_stops_the_daemon_like_sigterm` now 129; test support's `stop` is FERB's
own stop (marker, then SIGTERM; exit 0 as before) and `signal_stop` an unasked one; ferb-device
`ferbs_own_stop_names_the_daemon_it_stops_and_the_start_clears_it` and
`a_starting_daemon_keeps_a_marker_naming_it_and_drops_any_other`; `every_installer_scenario_matches_python` passes;
scripts/tests `test_the_service_definition_restarts_every_exit_but_ferbs_own`, and the bundle test's SIGTERM writes
the marker first. Ran: ferb-device all, ferbd lifecycle, services, native_host, every_method_answers, chat_replay.

**Turn FERB off from Settings (APP-1110 owner, APP-1111 ruling).** After this change nothing the owner could reach
stopped FERB completely: the owner had to have FERB stopped by hand for an exam whose proctoring app wouldn't start
beside it. His words: "hmm lets hide it in settigns???". Settings → General has a "Turn off" section: the button

open FERB.app again.", and while tasks run the question "A task is running. Stop it and turn FERB off?" ("N tasks

`~/.ferb/service.off`, sends `launchctl kill SIGTERM gui/<uid>/com.ferb.daemon`, waits up to 15 s for the pid to

again." The pid marker alone wasn't enough: launchd's RunAtLoad starts the daemon again at the next login, so the
file persists and the daemon exits 0 at its start while it exists ("turned off in FERB's Settings: starts again when
FERB.app opens" in its log), and exits 0 on any signal. FERB.app removes the file first thing in
`applicationDidFinishLaunching`, before its service read; the launch then finds the daemon not running and runs its
usual quiet update (AppSetupPlan.decide → .update → `setup --service --update` → kickstart). `Installer::install`

both read in code, not run. The root power helper (com.ferb.power, KeepAlive) is not stopped. Tests: ferbd

start exits 0 without serving, the file stays, serving again once it's gone); NotchCore `TurnOffPlanTests` (the

## 2026-11-22 · 165 · FERB knows when the Mac, not FERB, kept it answering: Power Nap's brief wakes, the sleep record, device.facts

**Why.** With the lid closed on power and insomnia mode off, the owner could still chat from the phone. The
coordinator read `pmset -g log` (2026-11-21 22:24–22:34): macOS's Power Nap woke the asleep Mac every 1–3 minutes
("DarkWake from Deep Idle … Using AC"). FERB's daemon answered during those wakes; FERB held nothing awake. The next
day he asked FERB from the phone how that was possible. FERB guessed that it had held the Mac awake itself. It said
it knew no "keep Mac on" setting, and that nothing in its records covered sleep or wake. Owner: "ok, so ferb should
knwo and tell user that its mac and not its service - can feb find it out itself??" (SENSE-426). On the first plan
(the facts in Layer 1 and Layer 2): "so is this all again in the prompt pile up?? and not in tools planner cna see???"
(SENSE-427).

**What FERB reads now, and from where.**
- `ferb_core::power::PowerReading` gains three fields, read by `ferb-platform-macos` `power::Facts`:
  - `dark_wake`: asleep and only briefly awake. Read from `IOPMConnectionGetSystemCapabilities`: the CPU bit without
    the graphics bit. 0x1f is a full wake, 0x19 a dark wake.
  - `power_nap_ac` and `power_nap_battery`: `IOPMCopyActivePMPreferences`, `DarkWakeBackgroundTasks` per power source.
  - Both functions are in IOPMLibPrivate.h (exported by IOKit, not in the public SDK). Unread means `None`, and nothing
    is said.
  - The power watch also takes `kIOMessageSystemCapabilityChange` (dark wake to full and back) as a change.
  - Read whenever asked: each read costs well under a millisecond. On this Mac: `dark_wake: Some(false)`, Power Nap on
    for both power sources.
- `ferb-mac-hands` `native::device` (device.facts' reading, one shared path) gains:
  - `hardware`: the device tree's product-name ("MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025)" here), the chip
    (`machdep.cpu.brand_string`) and memory (`hw.memsize`). Never a serial number.
  - The output device's kind, from CoreAudio's transport type and, for the built-in device, its data source: speakers,
    headphones, built_in, bluetooth, usb, display, airplay or other. No name is added: the existing `audio_output` name
    stays as SENSE-422 had it.
  - Each display's `built_in`, and `external_displays`.
  - All of it is read on each device.facts call, as before.
- The insomnia area (`ferb-daemon` `insomnia.rs`) follows the Mac's sleep whether the mode is on or off:
  - It journals `mac.power` (SENSE-429): `asleep` at a sleep from a full wake (lid, power source, Power Nap), `awake`
    at the full wake (since when, and how many brief wakes), and lid and power-source changes between looks.
  - A brief wake is counted, not journaled: a night is two rows, not some 700.
  - FERB first seeing a brief wake (it started during the night) records `found`. A wake whose kind can't be read ends
    the sleep and is never counted as brief.
  - `mac.power` joins STORE-401's operational journal kinds (90 days, `operational_days`), as `mac.back_in_use` is.

**Where it is said** (SENSE-427: behind the read tool; the context gains one line, only while it is true).
- `device.facts` (`ferbd` `compose/device.rs`; a planner lookup and a worker tool). It adds `hardware`,
  `audio_output_kind` and `external_displays`. It adds `power`: fully awake or asleep in a brief wake, `asleep_since`
  and `brief_wakes_since`, lid, power source, Power Nap plugged in and on battery, and what Power Nap means for FERB.
  It adds `keep_my_mac_working`: on, since, what the mode is, and, when off, what FERB keeps awake (idle sleep only
  while a task runs with the lid open; never a closed Mac) and whether it does so now. With the mode on, it says
  whether a closed Mac on battery is kept working (the helper).
- New arguments `since`/`until` (ISO dates or date-times, trail.query's `time_bound`) add `sleep_record`: the
  `mac.power` and `insomnia.state` rows of that stretch, in words, oldest first, at most 300. A malformed one is the
  caller's ValueError before anything is read.
- The catalog addition's description and schema changed (`catalog_additions.json`, still SENSE-422's row); Python's
  frozen `tools.json` is untouched.
- The live facts: only while `dark_wake` is true, one line after this Mac's line (`mac_now::context_line`, through
  `facts_line`'s new `asleep` part). Otherwise nothing is added: no fixture or recorded scenario changes.
- `insomnia.status` (on and off, so `chat.status` too) carries `asleep` and `asleep_line`. `ferb-mobile`'s
  `Insomnia` and the FFI record carry them (UniFFI defaults: false, none).
- Both phone apps (`MacAsleep.line`/`.waiting`): the Mac's line comes first under the tabs while the last status says
  so and the link hasn't stopped for good. A message waiting for the Mac then reads "Your Mac is asleep; this goes when
  it wakes." No notification: the brief wakes come and go every few minutes. Files: Android `MacAsleep.kt` and
  `ui/Main.kt`; iOS `MacAsleep.swift` and `FerbAppUI/Tabs.swift`. Nothing touched in MainActivity or the privacy
  cover.

**New words.**
- The owner (phone status, `asleep_line`):
  - "Your Mac is asleep with its lid closed. It wakes for a moment now and then, so replies can take a few minutes,
    and anything that needs its screen waits until you open it."
  - "Your Mac is asleep. It wakes for a moment now and then, so replies can take a few minutes, and anything that
    needs its screen waits until it's awake."
- The models (the context line while asleep): "- This Mac is asleep[ with its lid closed][, on power|, on
  battery][ since HH:MM[ (as far as FERB saw)]]: macOS's Power Nap wakes it briefly now and then | macOS woke it
  briefly in the background, and FERB runs only during those wakes, so replies can take minutes and anything that
  needs the screen, keyboard or pointer waits until the Mac is opened | woken; FERB's Keep my Mac working mode is
  on|off; device.facts has the details and the sleep record".
- device.facts' new texts: `mac_now::POWER_NAP_ABOUT`, `MODE_ABOUT`, `OUTSIDE_MODE`, `HISTORY_ABOUT`, the `awake` and
  `closed_lid_on_battery` values, `compose/device.rs` `RECORD_EMPTY`, and the record's event words ("went to sleep",
  "found asleep (FERB started or missed the sleep)", "woke fully", "lid closed", "lid opened", "unplugged: on

**Also fixed (found reading DMN-614's path).** During insomnia mode, a Mac that sleeps anyway (closed on battery
without the helper) gets Power Nap wakes. Each one's end held macOS's sleep for 2 s, published "your Mac is going to

**Named differences.** `retention::OPERATIONAL_KINDS` gains `mac.power`: ferb-store `the_rule_tables_are_python_s`

**Evidence.**

## 2026-11-22 · 166 · The memory-import lab ported: what was typed, one profile kept in place, the work log, and the owner's new flow

**What.** The owner's memory-import lab (`~/Desktop/ferb-memory-import-lab`, 2026-11-10, read only) is ported into the
Rust engine, with his flow of 2026-11-22 (MEM-447, MEM-448).
- **Readers** (ferb-memory). Claude Code and Codex are read from what the owner typed: `~/.claude/history.jsonl`
  and `~/.codex/history.jsonl` (`import_local`, MEM-432). There is one conversation per session-day, so a later
  read pays only for new days (MEM-433). Codex's folder comes from its session file's first 64 KB. Claude Code's
  saved notes are still read, as claims. claude.ai's manifest export is read from exactly the parts it names, and
  exports get plain checks (`import_exports`, MEM-438).
- **Reading and placing** (ferb-learning).
  - A run reads three chunks at once (MEM-434). It keeps checked facts with where each was said
    (`memory_import_facts`, migration 0067, MEM-436) and places them into the profile afterwards (`place`, MEM-439,
    MEM-450). A line is a memory item whose name and id never change. A join credits the day; an update is a new
    version only when it is newer and different. The owner's corrections are read from the item (MEM-442).
  - Scope is set by the line's words (MEM-443) and shown in the item's about, as is "last said …" for old lines.
    Offers are checked against the work log and newer lines (MEM-446). Offers 30-60 days old are asked about once,
    at most five (MEM-444). A recent repeat holds up at once (`CoreProfile::holds_up`, MEM-445).
  - The one notice is the profile's report (`tell_done_with`). An export FERB fetched is deleted when its import is
    done, or a day after a failure (MEM-440). An older export sends nothing (MEM-438).
- **Work log** (`worklog.rs`, MEM-441). Entries are learned nodes of kind `work_log` (key `tool/session/day`, the id
  as `thread_id`), dated by the session's day, written by `memory/worklog.md` and found by `memory.learned`.
- **Daemon.**
  - At chat.attach after `setup.finished`, FERB asks about the coding assistants it finds (`memory_local`). On Yes it
    imports, tells the owner and keeps up hourly, quietly; the Settings switch is `memory.local_import`. Then it asks
    about the websites (`memory_sites`), offering the browsing profiles.
  - Choosing a profile makes two quiet watches. Each is a schedule every 15 minutes until met, with the profile in its
    recorded scope and the `job` target. A watch posts only a failed run or one with gaps, once (MEM-451).
  - The workers' `memory.import` tool (a catalog addition after `browser.downloads`) takes only paths under FERB's
    downloads folder. `memory.import.scope` and `memory.import.offer` record the owner's word.
- **The ask (MEM-452).** After an import's notice, the offers 30-60 days old and the lines from a while ago go in one
  numbered list. It is FERB's own question (`memory_offers`, capability `memory.offers`), routed like a task's
  question, so the owner's next message answers it. `import_answer.md` reads which numbers his words mean; code applies
  that to the offers and lines; FERB says what it did in one line.
- **Every own question goes through the real table (MEM-453).** `memory_local` and `memory_sites` were missing from
  `steering::memory_questions`, so the real gateway would have refused them (KeyError), while group A's stand-in let
  them through. They are in it now, as is `memory_offers`. `ask_owner` itself refuses a kind the table doesn't take.
  The contract test `ferb-daemon/tests/own_question_kinds.rs` reads every own-question call site from the code.

  it applies (with Change: Everywhere / Only in a project…) and its offer (Still on / Done / No thanks), through the new
  `memory.import.lines` RPC (private on a phone) and `.scope`/`.offer` (sensitive).
- **memory.learned** names the work log in its description (`tool_changes.json`, MEM-441).

## 2026-11-22 · 167 · The site asks for Google sign-in before the download; the owner's user list, unsubscribe and update mail

**What.** On the owner's word (REL-433) the site's download now starts with Continue with Google; the how is REL-434,
which supersedes REL-413 (the site is no longer static only) while keeping its look and its script-free pages.
- `site/index.html`: the download section's button is Continue with Google (`/api/auth/google?file=…`), with one line
  under it: "Signing in means FERB may email you about important updates, each with a one-click unsubscribe." The
  "your data" line now says FERB has no server for your tasks, history and memory (the site now keeps a sign-in list).
- `site/api` (Vercel Functions, Node, ESM, no build step; shared code in `api/_lib`, which Vercel doesn't serve as
  functions): `auth/google` (state, nonce, PKCE in a signed 10-minute HttpOnly cookie), `auth/callback` (openid-client
  checks Google's answer; a download sign-in records email, name and first sign-in and shows a page whose meta
  refresh starts the download through a 10-minute signed link), `download` (behind `/download/:file`, now a rewrite
  instead of a redirect; records the last download and sends 302 to the release file), `unsubscribe` (GET from the
  email's link, POST from the mail app's one-click button), `admin` (only a verified Google account in ADMIN_EMAILS,
  8-hour cookie; list, counts and CSV with formula cells defused).
- The list: one Neon Postgres table `ferb_users` (email, name, first_signin_at, last_download_at, unsubscribed), made
  on first use. Signing in again changes only the name, so an unsubscribe is never undone.
- Mail: `site/scripts/send-update.mjs` (Resend's REST API, one email at a time, idempotency key per person and
  update, List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers). A dry run unless `--send`; `--test-to` sends to one
  address. Nothing was sent.
- `site/privacy.html`: a section on what the website keeps, why, where (Neon for Vercel, Resend) and its two cookies.
- `site/env.example` names the settings (not `.env.example`: the commit gate refuses `.env.*` files). The setup guide
  for the owner is outside the repo, at `~/Desktop/FERB-site-signin-setup.md`.
- Pins: openid-client 6.8.9, @neondatabase/serverless 1.2.0, locked in `site/package-lock.json`; node_modules is not
  committed. Node 24 on Vercel.

**Why the DMG link is not a lock.** Sparkle downloads the same DMG from `/updates/files/…` and GitHub's public release
(REL-430, REL-432), and that must stay public so updates never need a sign-in. So the sign-in is the site's front door:
the site never hands out a lasting file address, but someone who digs out the release's GitHub address can still
download without signing in. Making the file itself private would mean hosting the DMG elsewhere; that is the
owner's call.

**Tests** (`node --test site/tests/*.test.mjs`, no install needed: every service is a stand-in; a new commit-level
gate check in `kb/gate.toml`, which needs a `Gate-change:` trailer). 29 pass:
- tokens: tampering, another secret, another purpose and expiry are refused;
- sign-in and download: the full flow with a stand-in Google; no download without a fresh link for that file; an
  expired, cancelled or unconfirmed sign-in records nobody; a database outage never blocks the download and nothing
  personal is logged;
- unsubscribe by link and by RFC 8058 POST; forged or other-purpose tokens change nothing;
- the admin gate: no cookie, a forged, expired, other-purpose or no-longer-listed cookie, an unverified or other
  account; escaping and CSV;
- the update feed: vercel.json still redirects `/updates/*` straight to the public releases, with no middleware or
  rewrite in front of it; the pages link no DMG directly.
openid-client 6.8.9 was also run offline against a stand-in token endpoint: the redirect_uri sent matches, the
claims come back, and a wrong state is refused.

**Unverified.** Nothing was deployed, and Google, Neon, Resend and Vercel were never called. Still to check live
(LIVE-1167): that Vercel runs `api/*.js` with named GET/POST exports and keeps `api/_lib` from becoming functions;

## 2026-11-22 · 171 · A stop's end shows once in the chat: the task's turn reads Cancelled

**The owner (ORCH-688):** "didnt you said you fixed this redundant response???" Read-only evidence in his
`~/.ferb/ferb.db` `chat_entries`: at 14:56:07 "stop" (request f65ce9b7…) got an answer from "reply" at 14:56:23.122
and the stopped task's own turn (request f8977104…, task a843aa54…) an answer from "task" at .139, both inline, both
"Stopped, as you asked. I'm not sure whether my last step on com.google.Chrome went through: …"; at 15:21:04 the same
for "ok lets call this assingmnt here. whats done is good rest lets not do" (requests ade21800… and afba3bbc…, task
0a59cf47…). His screenshot of the 15:21 case: the bubble, the seek.onlinedegree.iitm.ac.in "Sent / From …" card and
the sites chip, once under the task's turn (with "Cancelled") and again under his stop message.

**Why both were filed (code at a2c30951).** ORCH-579's chat stop: control.rs:936-939 sets the tree's
`stop_told_in` to the stop's request; the task's end is composed with `told_in` (control.rs:636-641 `told_in`, from
tree.rs:3537 and card.rs:579) and sent on the task's own stream (tree.rs:671/675); then the stop's reply is that same
recorded end, words and cards (control.rs:991-1013, `stop_told`). On the clients `told_in` only kept the end from also
being posted *below* (APP-825): FERB.app ConversationArchive.applyOutcome still put the end's lines and cards on the
task's turn and `finish` its answer (ConversationArchive.swift:1165; `guard toldElsewhere.remove(id)` at :1178 stops
only the reply below), and ChatProjector the same (entries.rs apply_outcome; finish's `turn.text = end.said` at
entries.rs:1340, `told_elsewhere` only in `placement`). So the words, the card and the chip were drawn twice, once on
each turn, on the Mac and on the phones (their fold reads the same entries). LIVE-860's pass said the opposite ("the
task's own message up the chat shows it stopped").

**The ruling (ORCH-689, APP-1113; APP-825 superseded).** One behaviour, the one LIVE-860 describes: the stop's reply
under his message carries the end (words, cards, sites); the task's own turn shows only that it ended (Cancelled, its
card or checklist). Shared path: `told_in` now means "that request's reply says this end". Both reducers
(ConversationArchive and ChatProjector, which mirror each other) note the end's words (`saidElsewhere` /
`said_elsewhere`) when an outcome carries `told_in`, skip its lines, note, cards and later answer, and `finish` files
those words on that turn as an empty answer with the end's status (no files, not verified); a turn that already
showed an answer gets nothing more. Either order of the reply and the end works. The fold, EntryFold and the phones
need nothing new: they draw an answer entry with no text as its status words.

`told_in` was also how a restart's first run is filed in place (ORCH-683), whose line no reply repeats: such an end
now carries `keeps_words: true` (TreeState `stop_keeps_words`), and the clients keep its words. The recorded Python
stop scenarios carry no new key (their bytes are unchanged).

Two edges where words could be left unsaid or said twice, closed in control.rs:
- A chat stop past its 10 s wait cleared `stop_told_in` while the end might already have been composed naming the
  reply. Composing an end with `told_in` now claims the reply (`stop_told_claimed`); the stop clears `told_in` only
  while unclaimed, under the tree's lock, else waits for that end and says it. `stop_told` refuses an end with
  `keeps_words`.
- A stop while a restart waits (ORCH-684) with the stopped run still finishing: its end, now the owner's stop, was
  filed in place with "Stopped, as you asked. This is where things stood: …" and the stop said "Stopped, as you
  asked." again. `call_off_restart` now points the end at one teller without `keeps_words`: a chat stop goes the chat
  stop's way (its reply waits for the end and says it; the retry's turn adds nothing); for the Stop button the
  retry's turn says the end (`stop_told`), else "Stopped, as you asked." as before.

**Routes checked.** A chat stop, a stop beside new work (ORCH-638: the stop's words in the new task's plan receipt,
the task's turn Cancelled), the Stop button and the phone's Stop (both `task.stop`: no reply tells it, the task's own

way, its full Messages requests already passing FERB's 127.0.0.1 relay (`claude/proxy.rs`). **The API loop**
(`api/mod.rs` `event_loop`) owns its request state and appends each result (`add_results`). Measured on a843aa54 (the
lagged deltas of its `model.usage` spans): a Chrome mac_snapshot 2.9 to 3.1 characters per token, 4,000 to 9,400
tokens; a screenshot about 2,050; small results about 170.

mac_screenshot with its image, browser/ferb_browser snapshot or screenshot) of the same kind and window or tab replaces

## 2026-11-22 · 176 · A new phone session proves the phone before it says online: no call meets a locked Mac

**What failed.** ferb-link's `tests/relay.rs` failed in the push gate today and on earlier pushes; the gate keeps 30
lines, so it named no test. Journal 161 had seen `own_relay_down_falls_back_to_the_shared_relay_and_comes_back` fail
once in 14 runs: `chat.send` answered `locked` at relay.rs:296, just after the own relay came back. That is the
only relay failure on record. My own runs below caught no relay failure: the Mac's load was 2 to 15 then, against
the gate's 133 and more.

**Why (a race in the product, not in the test).** `Phone::serve` (ferb-link client.rs) set the phase online and only
then spawned the presence proof (`link.challenge`, the device key's signature, `link.present`) for a new connection
that had not moved (`moved != Some(true)`). The Mac (the stand-in, as the daemon's gate) gives a connection the
phone's unlock only once it proved the device key (SEC-26: `open_window` needs `present` for the device's window).
A call made the moment the phase said online raced that spawned task. Under load the task ran late, and the call
was refused `locked`. The test waits for `phase == online && tier == own_relay` and calls `chat.send` at once, so it
lost the race now and then. A start-over (PHN-225) already proved the key on the new connection before the session
moved ("so no call ever meets a locked Mac in between"); a fresh connection after a drop did not. The phones have
the same gap: ferb-mobile-ffi proved presence on a thread of its own after it heard online, and the core syncs on
coming online. PHN-684 made only the unlock statement wait for that proof. I infer, without a phone, that a phone
back from a relay change could have its first sync or a waiting message refused as locked until the next sync.

**Fix (PHN-799).** `Phone::online` calls `prove_on` on the welcomed connection before `serve`, the same function a
start-over uses: with an in-process signer by itself, otherwise through the app's `prove` event (3 s at most; no
answer: online unproved, as before). `serve` takes `moved` and `proved` apart. The phase's `proved` is now true for
every proven session, and the old spawned proof runs only for a session that came online unproved.
ferb-mobile-ffi `present` sends no second proof for a proved session. It marks that session as presented and
settled, so `wait_presented` (PHN-684) has nothing to wait for and the open-app presence loop (PHN-648) keeps going.
If the app is open it sends its active presence at once, as the per-session proof used to carry it.

**Tests.**
- New `tests/link.rs a_call_made_the_moment_a_new_session_is_online_meets_the_phones_unlock`: the stand-in answers
  `phone.present` 1.5 s late (new `Standin::set_present_delay`). Three times the phone goes to the background and
  back, and a `tasks.list` is made the moment the phase says online with a new session number. Built against the
  old client.rs, it fails every run in round 1 with `locked` (0.39 s). With the fix it passes (4.9 s).
- relay.rs fallback test: the session that comes back on the own relay says `proved` before its `chat.send`.
- The relay binary the gate's way (ferb-test-guard, `--test-threads 3`, `--nocapture`), one run after another at
  nice 19 with no extra load. The Mac's load average was 2 to 15 then; the gate's was 133 and more. Fixed: 10
  consecutive passes on a2c30951 (two from a first build, then eight from the final one). One more pass came inside
  the whole ferb-link suite, which passed entirely.
  Without the fix (the binary built from a2c30951 as it was), 9 runs in turn with those passed too: at this load the
  race was not caught that way. The new link test above catches it on every run.
- ferb-mobile-ffi's whole suite and ferb-link's whole suite pass under the guard. fmt and clippy are clean (ferb-link
  with devrelay, ferb-mobile-ffi, -D warnings).
- After rebasing on 01b9622b, which touched ferb-link and ferb-mobile-ffi: fmt and clippy are clean again, both whole
  suites pass again (relay included), and the relay binary passed 3 more runs in a row. That makes 15 passes of the
  relay binary with the fix and no failure.

**Unverified.**
- No real phone ran this. The app path (the `prove` event before online, the active presence on a proved session)
  is covered only by ferb-mobile-ffi's own tests.
- The whole workspace gate (fmt, lint, test, portable) was not run, and neither were ferb-mobile's tests (that crate
  is unchanged).
- A new connection now goes online after two more round trips (the challenge and the proof), plus the app's
  signature on a phone. It is not measured on a real relay.

  batches placed of batches: `import_profile::place` now publishes one `placing` event per batch, and one at the end.
  Parts left unread are said with what happens next. Each active website watch becomes a row from its records: a run
  under way now (the daemon's `schedule_runs`); when it asked (the first `schedule.quiet`/`posted` with status done:
  the request has the first run ask, so a run that went well first is when the export was asked for); whether its last
  run needed him; its next run. Times are "at 23:40", "yesterday at …", "tomorrow at …" or "on Nov 3 at …". When an
  import of a watched site runs, its row replaces the watch's. Code facts only; no model's words decide a stage.
- **Daemon** (`areas_a::memory_import`). A `Tell::Always` run registers at its start (`begin`), turns to placing
  before `place_run`, and leaves when its notice is said (`ended`), so the notice is the one message. A cancel ends it
  on its own event. The hourly pass's quiet updates never show. `refresh` publishes the card on the new telemetry
  topic `memory.import.live` (`{"card": … | null}`) when it changes. `memory.import.status` gains `live` only while
  there is a card, so the recorded transcript (`{"current": null, "runs": []}`) is unchanged. A watch's run start and
  end (`schedules::run_schedule`), the websites' answer and the daemon's start (`resume`) refresh it.
- **Phones.** ferbd keeps the last card published (its group A publish wrapper) and hands it to the phone gate
  (`Phones::set_memory_import`). The phone's `chat.status` carries it as `memory_import`, removed with the other
  words while a phone is locked without words. The bridge's status poll pushes it on change. ferb-mobile reads it as
  `PhoneStatus.memory_import: Option<ImportCard>` (`ImportRow::fraction`, `names_rows`), and the FFI mirrors
  `ImportCard`, `ImportRow` and `PhoneStatus.memoryImport` (default none).
- **FERB.app.** `MemoryImportCard` (NotchCore) is read from the bus event, from `memory.import.status` at attach,
  and again on `bus.dropped`. It is drawn as a transcript row (`TranscriptRow.memoryImport`) after the open questions,
  today only (`inlineMemoryImport`). `MemoryImportCardView` is a sibling of the turn card on the black glass: the
  caption, the stage line, a 5 pt capsule bar that eases out over 0.7 s (and is set at once under Reduce Motion), the
  count, "found so far", a quieter detail, and an amber note. There is no spinner. The Memory page shows the same card
  at its top, and under "Import from other assistants" each source's last run (`MemoryImportLastRun`). It polls every
  2 s while a card or run is live.
- **Android and iPhone** (one design). The card is a stateless component in `:design` (`components/ImportCard.kt`)
  and in FerbDesign (`MemoryImport.swift`). It is a sibling of the parts card: radius 22, a 6 pt bar, and a 650 ms
  ease-out `progress` curve, added to the shared motion table (`motion.json`, `Motion.kt`, `Motion.swift`). It snaps
  under reduced motion. Each app's chat model now decides its rows in one place (`ChatModel.shown`: the earlier
  link, today's rows, the open-question boxes, then the card, keyed `memory-import`). It is never in the earlier days
  and never a stored row.

- **The phones' home page (MEM-457).** The owner approved the screenshots: "approved, yes show it on the home page
  too". On a new day with nothing said yet the Chat tab is the home page (PHN-626); it now shows the same card above
  the message box while an import runs, through a `live` slot on the design's `HomePage` (Android `Pages.kt`, iPhone
  `MobileScreens.swift`; none by default, so the design's goldens are unchanged). The phone goldens' FERB reply is now
  the real line ("Thanks! I'm reading through Claude Code now and I'll tell you what I learned.").
- **The last month (MEM-458, superseding MEM-401).** The owner: "btw i want a switch of this memeory trnasfer of both
  local and website. since it will take a lottt of usage - i thik i wont ship it in the real app, OR im thinking to
  cap it at 1 month for both local and website - i thikn this is better". `import_sources::WINDOW_MONTHS` is 1.
  `ReadOptions.months` and `ImportJob.window_months` carry it, so the import, its estimate and the work log all read
  the last calendar month. Python's three (`PYTHON_WINDOW_MONTHS`) are kept only for the recordings.
- **Two switches (MEM-459).** The new RPC `memory.import.switch {which: local | sites, on}` is group A's, the CLI
  role's, and sensitive on a phone (the fingerprint):
  - The coding assistants (`memory.local_import`, now the one switch). On reads them now and keeps up hourly. Off
    reads nothing and stops the update: a run under way is aborted through its abort handle (`State.local_abort`) and
    ended as cancelled, and `local_update` checks the switch between sources and before the work log.
  - ChatGPT and Claude (`memory.sites_import`, a new setting). On asks which browser profile, as at setup:

    through `schedule_change` and ends a run of those sources; the 24-hour deletion of a fetched file (MEM-440) still

**What.** On 2026-11-22/23 the owner's Claude Code import put 42 of his imported lines in always on by itself, each
told by its own "Now always on: “…” (FERB's understanding)" notice with a Remembered card (read-only, his

are facts" (MEM-462). On the screenshots he said "approve", with Keep / Remove for items already on (MEM-464).

  `memory.import` journal row, or is an import line's item) holds up only when its line says `approved` (his word) or
  `on` (an earlier build's join waiting for his word). So neither `saved`'s join at once nor the weekly pass can place
  it. IMP-47's recent repeat now only makes a line `suggested`. `CoreProfile::keep` makes an Approve his pin where the
  entry stands (no move, so the settled prompt stays).
- **The review** (new `ferb-learning/src/import_review.rs`). One list in three parts, each its own question and
  buttons: keep in mind all the time (grouped: how you like me to work, about you, your setup), are these still true,
  still want help with these. `review()` is what every client draws; `answer_review(profile, part, ids, answer)` is
  the one path the buttons, the Memory page's Always on / Not always on (`profile_word`) and his typed words
  (`apply_answer`, now read against the list as it stands) all go through. `suggest_always_on` marks lines after every
  placement and at the start; an earlier build's joins become `on`, his own pins `approved`. Older lines asked about

  ask was converted, and again after a typed answer that leaves items; restored with its id at a restart; closed

  → `ChatLog::fold_notices`: every notice whose ref is `memory-always-on-<id>` for any version of an imported line's

## 2026-11-23 · 181 · Sending into an editor's terminal, a refused send said, roomier tabs, a calm session screen

**What failed (the owner's verdict, PHN-800).** On FERB.app 202611221757 he sent from his Moto to a Claude Code session
running in VS Code's integrated terminal (this checkout, `claude --resume 0060c0a4-…`). Read only: `phone_audit`
in `~/.ferb/ferb.db`, 2026-11-22 23:43 to 23:45:
- `sessions.send` at 23:43:55 answered ok. It was the Mac's question (`needs_yes`, GATE-622), not a delivery, so
  nothing was typed then.
- `sessions.control` at 23:44:01 and 23:44:08 were refused -32045 (NOT_THE_SESSION). The journal's
  `sessions.control` rows show his control was taken both times (`take_control`). The refusal came from the send
  inside it: `deliver` maps any foreground error to NOT_THE_SESSION (ferb-daemon sessions/mod.rs, the
  `.map_err(|e| no(codes::NOT_THE_SESSION, e))` after `foreground`).
- Every later `sessions.send` (23:44:12 to 23:44:37) was refused -32045 the same way.

**Why: which proof, and what VS Code shows.**
- The proof list was `[title, folder]`, but `foreground` in ferbd compose/sessions.rs used only `f.proof.first()`:
  the session's title, "FERB Rust migration research review" (its `ai-title`).
- I read VS Code's Accessibility tree read only (AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue, nothing set, focused or pressed),
  with VS Code in front because the owner was working in it. The focused element is xterm.js's input: an AXTextField
  with DOM class `xterm-helper-textarea` and description "Terminal 1, 2.1.330 Run the command: Toggle Screen Reader
  Accessibility Mode…". Its containers carry the classes `terminal xterm`, `integrated-terminal` and id `terminal`,
  in a window titled "FERB-site-signin-setup.md — FERB". The session's title is nowhere.
- "2.1.330" is the agent's program as macOS names it. Claude Code's own installer runs
  `~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.330`, and VS Code's tab title is `${process}`.
- So the proof failed every time. VS Code was brought forward, then the app that was in front was put back. Nothing
  was typed anywhere: the proof comes before any typing, and `phone_audit` has no successful send.

**Fix (HAND-682).**
- Typing needs a terminal by structure (ferb-policy's `surface`: a terminal app, or xterm.js's classes) that is
  provably the session's. Either its title is in the element's or window's words, or its program is in the terminal's
  own words (below the window; the window's title too in a terminal app) with its folder in the window's.
  `ferb-sessions::proof` (portable) decides this.
- The daemon offers program and folder only when no other running session in the same app shares both
  (`proof_of`); two alike are proven by the title alone.
- When the focus isn't proven (say the cursor is in the editor), ferbd finds the one window of the app whose title
  names the folder and raises it. In that window, the one text input whose own words name the program gets the
  cursor (`ax.focus`), and the proof is read again. Several inputs naming it: no cursor moved, refused.
- The refusal says why: not in a terminal, or not this session's.

**When no terminal proves itself the session's (HAND-683, the owner: "ok go without it. with a fallbakc so that
user can chose themselves").** One shared path for every host:
- FERB types nothing. The session lists the terminals FERB can see in that app: the one in front now (when the focus
  is a terminal), then every terminal in its windows by structure, by the app's own words ("config.toml — blog ·
  Terminal 2, zsh"). The refusal is `choose_terminal` (-32049).
- The phones and FERB.app show "Which terminal is this session in?", the Mac's reason, those terminals, and
  Don't send. His pick goes with `sessions.control` (`terminal`, signed by the fingerprint on a phone).
- The daemon keeps it for that session's process while he controls it. ferbd finds it again (that window's n-th
  terminal with the same words), focuses it, proves the focus is that element, and checks again right before
  typing. If it changed, FERB types nothing and asks again.

**Every kind of session: what identifies its terminal (asked by the owner, read only on his Mac).** The identity
every terminal session has is the agent's tty and pid. What each host shows of it:

| Host | Handle | Proof | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terminal | `tty of tab` | built: AppleScript by tty | Automation |
| iTerm2 | `tty`, `unique id` | AppleScript, `write text` | a small bridge |
| tmux | `pane_tty` | built | none |
| WezTerm, kitty | CLI lists | `cli send-text` | kitty needs remote control on |
| VS Code family | none from outside (no pid or tty in Accessibility; the pid only in a hover tooltip; `state.vscdb` holds VS Code's own terminal ids, not OS pids) | HAND-682, else HAND-683 | an extension for exact background sends (T-1295) |
| JetBrains | none from outside | the same | a plugin (T-1295) |
| Ghostty, Warp, Alacritty, Zed, others | none | the same | none |
| Chat apps | the window id | built (HAND-672) | none |
| Codex | its thread id | built (app-server) | none |

**A refused send on the phones (PHN-800).** Both phones: a refused send, or a refused control after the Yes,
closes the question (before, it stayed open: "im stuck"). The words leave the box into a dimmed bubble after the
last line, with "Not sent." and the Mac's own reason, and Try again, which sends the same words the same way. A
send that goes through removes the bubble. Nothing optimistic is shown: a message appears as sent only when the
agent's record has it.

**Tabs (PHN-800, then PHN-801).** The owner found the 36-wide tabs too close, then said "i want teh names" of the
icon-only bar. Three layouts were drawn on both phones at 360/375 and normal widths: the link dot inside the bar,

- The chosen tab shows its icon and name. The other four share what is left beside one round button: the lab's 46

- The connection's state is a badge on the profile button. Its sheet is now the profile page's first row: the mark,

**Session screen (PHN-800).**

- The "…" menu is a white card. It shows where the session runs, then Watch, Hand to FERB, Stop its turn (while it

Owner 2026-11-23, on FERB.app 202611222206 after answering the import review with Approve all: "its blank after i

no composer. Reopening and relaunching the app didn't help. On his phone the review stayed as a plain question card
with no list. The website import's card said "I check your email every 15 minutes". Two ChatGPT watch tasks asking
him were listed under Running.

**What his store and logs show (read only).**
- Today (2026-11-23) holds 47 notices in his chat history and no turns. 44 are "Now always on" notices the engine
  folded into the review (MEM-461). Every notice was said after the previous day's last turn (`afterTurnID`).
- After launch the app reads only today's page. I ran that page through `HistoryEntry.read`, `absorb` and
  `transcript(on:)` in a throwaway test: 31 entries decoded, 0 failed, 0 shown.

  (`memory.profile_changed`); the rest were on already. `review_settled` set the question aside: its
  `memory_questions` row is gone. Nothing was published, so its chat entry stayed `open`.

  is read by the body's layout, its greeting and its height. APP-1114.

## 2026-11-23 · 184 · The check is never run twice: FERB's own look, at most 6 calls, a small call for "not done"

**What.** The owner was shown an audit of his checks (11-09..11-23, 203 checks in his three stores: the check was 8% of
input tokens but 41% of uncached input, about 209k input tokens a check; the no-look rerun repeated its verdict 15 of
16 times and replaced it, dropping the first run's findings, tasks c252e651 and a2653; a not-done report's full check
agreed 49 of 50 times; one check ran 33 model calls). He asked "they sound good, but are they??? also what exactly
changes does this make?? is it a downgrade?", said "yes" to building three changes with a replay, and after the replays
chose "yes ship 2": ship the safe changes, keep the full context, park the slim one (ORCH-694, superseding ORCH-671;
PRM-370 supersedes PRM-359). The check's context is unchanged: every recorded call in full, as before.
- **No full re-check (ORCH-696).** Before the check, `attempt.rs::fresh_look` reads the place of the step's last
  acting call (ORCH-671's `last_action_at`): the tab's snapshot in its browser family, else the app's `mac.snapshot`
  (its window when named), through `Daemon::probe_read` (the gateway's observe-only probe, under the step's task);
  recorded as `verify.look` on the check and handed in as "FERB's fresh look" (`evidence::fresh_look_block`), which
  counts as the check's own look. No rerun: an outward met with no look at all, or a met with a changed file not read,
  is can't tell at once (`no_place_look`, `no_file_look`; one `verify.refused`). Where reruns remain (the Python
  recordings' path) the rerun's findings join the first run's by quote (`merged`): the c252e651 bug.
- **The cap (ORCH-696).** The check's token carries `max_calls = CHECK_CALLS` (6) through
  `WorkerHost::issue_token_capped` and `RunOptions::max_calls`; the gateway refuses calls past it with the check's own
  words (`CHECK_CALLS_SPENT`, for a capped grant naming no tools) and doesn't answer a capped check's repeat from
  ORCH-557's planner cache; RUN-445's wrong-call cap ends a run that keeps calling, and the check is unconfirmed.
- **The not-done router (ORCH-697).** `judge()` sends a not-done (not cancelled) report that ORCH-654 doesn't skip to
  `route_not_done`: one call on the checker's runtime (the task's switch honoured), mode supervisor, no tools, prompt
  `not_done.md`, one protected block (goal, conditions, the report, its last failed call redacted, attempt number,
  CHECK_IN_AFTER, the owner's answers in this step). retry, ask and fail come back as a check's `Next`, so ORCH-650 and
  the 5-attempt check-in hold; a failed or malformed answer ends the step as reported (`verify.routed` records it). The
  full check still runs when FERB's guard stopped the attempt (ORCH-691; its stop carried in `TreeState::stuck_taken`)
  or an owner_step fact stands (ORCH-690).
- **The seam.** `Daemon::lean_check()` (true; ferbd's `Reads::lean_check` true, the stand-ins' script false,
  seams-off.txt) keeps the earlier check for replays of Python recordings.

**Prompts changed.** verifier.md, four PRM-370 edits (named in `engine/fixtures/catalog/prompt_changes.json`): "What you
get" names FERB's fresh look; a line on the check's few calls of its own; after acting, FERB's look counts as the
check's own and without one the pass is can't tell; a changed file not read makes a met can't tell. New

## 2026-11-23 · 187 · A temporary chat: no prior context, nothing kept, on and off by one dashed bubble

Owner 2026-11-23, in five messages (ORCH-699, ORCH-700, PHN-819, PHN-820). He asked for one switch in code that sends no context, with
an optional context field he can fill in later, so it could be used for a "temporary chat" with all the tools but no
prior context. Told it would only be made possible, he said "build it, its just a click on phones and mac". Then he
corrected the brief: the same small icon that turns it on turns it off, as in ChatGPT's and Claude's apps.

**The switch (engine, ORCH-701).**
- A temporary chat's conversation is `temporary:<id>`. Each of its messages gets a request id `temporary-<id>`, and
  its tasks keep that request id (ferb-core `temporary`). So every route and every store reader can tell from the id
  alone.
- `Inner::fresh_for(request_id)` (flow/temporary.rs) is the one switch. It is read by:
  - the planner (turn.rs `supervise`, `planner_blocks`);
  - every worker and checker run (ferb-worker's `WorkerHost::system`, `with_newly_always_on` and `issue_token` now get
    the run's task);
  - the question resolver (answer.rs);
  - the worker's context (attempt.rs: no relevant activity, no memory push).
- What such a turn doesn't get:
  - the Tier 1 profile (`system_for_request` blanks `identity_context`);
  - anything newly always on;
  - memory or the owner's activity;
  - the since-your-last-message and earlier-run blocks;
  - other chats' tasks (`task_state` lists only the temporary chat's own; the kept chat never lists a temporary one).
- What it gets: a code fact first (`FRESH_FACT`: nothing from before, nothing kept, don't promise to remember), with
  the owner's `extra_context` when given (origin owner).
- Lookups and tools:
  - The planner keeps only `about.read`, `about.diagnostics` and `device.facts`.
  - A run's token names every tool except `memory.read`, `memory.learned`, `chat.history`, `trail.query` and
    `trail.days`, and except tools that are offered only when named. The gateway refuses the rest (admit.rs reads the
    token's list; that file is unchanged).
  - Safety is unchanged: gateway, confirmations, sink rule, redaction, protection lists.

**Held in memory, nothing kept (ORCH-702).**
- The daemon holds one temporary chat (`TemporaryChats`). Its entries are made by the kept chat's own projector
  (`ChatProjector`), in memory, so clients fold them with their existing entry fold.
- RPC (fields added, ENG-14):
  - `chat.send` takes `fresh` and `extra_context`. A fresh send starts the chat if it is off. Its ack adds `fresh` and
    `conversation`, and never carries `entry_id`.
  - `chat.temporary.get` reads the chat.
  - `chat.temporary.set {on}` is the icon. `on` is required: a call without it is refused, never treated as a default.
  - `chat.status` carries `temporary` while one is on. Its approvals and running rows of the temporary chat carry
    `temporary: true`.
  - The bus topic `chat.temporary` says each change.
  - ferb-rpc: both methods are app_only (`TEMPORARY_ADDITIONS`). Phone classes: get is private, set is plain.
- Never written:
  - chat entries or submissions;
  - `task_results`, so the chat is not in the Tasks page (`TaskResults::page` leaves `temporary-` requests out), not
    in chat.status results and not in "since";
  - a `task.result` on the bus;
  - remember or forget side entries;
  - episodes (`record_episode`, `capture_after_outcome`);
  - the conversation index (ferb-memory `index_chat`);
  - day summaries (ferb-learning `summary.rs`).
- The journal's conversation rows, the task context and the continuity row are what the supervisor works from while
  a turn runs. `temporary::forget` deletes them in three cases: when the chat ends, when a task of an ended chat
  finishes, and at every start (`recover_after_restart`).
- A restart ends the chat. Its plans don't resume, and nobody is asked to pick its tasks up.
- Kept, as for any task:
  - `tasks` and their spans (the traces, which hold the model calls' text);
  - the gateway's ledger and confirmations;
  - the journal's audit rows (rule 6);
  - identifiers sealed from his words (GATE-604);
  - schedules and reminders it made.

**Clients.**
- FERB.app (APP-1122):
  - The dashed bubble sits beside the profile button in the notch header and in the window header.
  - The banner replaces the Today/History row.
  - The temporary chat is held in `NotchModel.temporaryChat`, separate from `conversation`, so nothing reaches
    chat.history.put or the archive.
  - It is read at each connect, on each `chat.temporary` event and from chat.status.
- Both phones (PHN-818):
  - ferb-mobile adds `temporary_chat`, `set_temporary_chat`, `send_temporary` (straight to the Mac, never the
    outbox), `last_temporary_chat`, `PhoneStatus.temporary`, the questions' and tasks' `temporary` flags and
    `Change::Temporary`, all in memory.
  - A locked status that leaves `temporary` out is never read as off.
  - Android and iPhone draw the same dashed bubble (FERB.app's geometry), left of the profile button on the chat tab.
  - They read the chat again on start, unlock, coming to the front and each status `rev`.
  - The iPhone never writes a temporary draft to scene storage.
- The phones' top bar adapts to its width (PHN-820). He said: "jsut pack them in a good looking hamburger icon if
  theres no space to show or place them ... contracat if really no space".
  - Width: the bar measures the window less its side insets (cutout and safe area), at the current text size.
  - Normal: the chosen tab with its name, the others at 36 or more, the bubble, the profile button.
  - Folded: when a tab would fall under 36, the bubble and the profile button fold into one three-line menu button.
    It carries the connection badge, and a dashed mark while the temporary chat is on. Its menu holds Temporary chat
    and This phone.
  - Contracted: if the bar is still too tight, the chosen tab drops its name.
  - Both phones use one layout rule: tab = (room − 8 − buttons×50 − chosen)/4.
  - At text size 1, Android folds at 360 and 320 and stays normal at 412. The iPhone stays normal at 375 and folds at
    320.
  - New string: `top_bar_more` "More" (the menu button's label).
- Which device shows it: every client, while it's on. It lives in the daemon's memory, so a relaunched app or an
  unlocked phone shows it, as the owner asked (ORCH-700).

**Strings (new).** "Temporary chat"; "End temporary chat"; "Temporary chat · FERB won't use what it knows or keep this
chat"; "This chat starts fresh. Tap the dashed bubble again to end it."; "Couldn't start a temporary chat. Try again.";

## 2026-11-23 · 190 · A temporary chat's planner no longer reads the kept chat, the schedules, the reminders or the screen

**What the owner saw (ORCH-699).** In a temporary chat he asked "but isnt your context off in this temp chat?? what
context did went to you?". FERB answered that it had received "the long prior conversation history, current
device/browser details, one schedule, one reminder, and a screenshot". His store (read only) confirmed it. The planner's
`model.turn` span (request `temporary-280cd51e…`, 09:35:41) had a 30,258-character context. It held:
- "Layer 5 — conversation" with 68 kept-chat entries: notices with no conversation (Mac sleep, heat, 46 "Now always on:
  …" memory notices), a scheduled run's result and a timer that went off;
- Layer 2's live facts, with his schedule (instructions included) and his reminder;
- his front window and its screenshot (`image_evidence`).

**Causes.** `fresh_for` was read where journal 187 put it, but four layers were built around it:
1. **The conversation.** history.rs `reserved` (and ferb-orchestrator `continuity::RESERVED_SESSIONS`) named only
   `schedule:` and `preview:`. ferb-core's temporary.rs already called the temporary chat "a reserved session, like
   `schedule:` and `preview:`", but neither list held it. So every notice with no conversation and every
   `schedule.posted` / `timer.delivered` row counted as the temporary chat's.
2. **The planner's live facts.** turn.rs called `live_facts(false, true)` for a fresh turn. The arguments are
   `(last_runs, owner_state)`, so `owner_state` was on, and with it the schedules, reminders and timers.
3. **Every role's instructions.** `system_inputs(live)` gave workers, checkers and the question resolver
   `live_facts(false, true)` (schedules and reminders) and `facts()` with memory's "When the owner says X, they
   mean Y". `system_for_request` blanked only the Tier 1 profile. The "not done" router and `worker_room` used
   `system_for`, which reads no request, so they also kept the profile.
4. **The screen.** `chat.send` captured the front window at send for every message. The capture reached the planner
   (front window block and image) and the workers (`start_image`).
- Also: Layer 6 listed every open question, the kept chat's included. The question resolver could route a temporary
  chat's answer to one of the kept chat's questions.

**The fix: the same switch, applied at each layer.**
- The conversation: `temporary:` is a reserved session in both lists. A temporary conversation now holds only its own
  messages and replies. Also, its tasks no longer reach the schedules' runs (`reaches_schedules`).
- The planner's live facts: `live_facts(false, false)`, as the intro's preview reads them.
- `Daemon::system_inputs(live, fresh)`. `system_for_request` passes `fresh_for(request)`, and `system_for` is that with
  no request. The "not done" router and `worker_room` now pass their request. ferbd's composition, when fresh:
  - facts from `environment::facts_with(…, memory=false)` (no time meanings, memory not read);
  - live facts without owner state;
  - no Tier 1 profile (not read).
- chat.rs: a fresh message's `screen` is false, so nothing is captured. No front window and no screenshot are taken,
  stored or sent. Its tools can still look at the screen when the request needs it.
- `Inner::question_in(session, task)`: in a temporary chat, only its own tasks' questions. This applies to the planner's
  Layer 6 and to the resolver's open list and routed approval.

**What a fresh turn's planner gets now.**

| Layer | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Fact first | FRESH_FACT (+ extra_context) | same |
| Layer 1 (macOS, paired profiles and their accounts, worker types) | yes | yes |
| Layer 5 conversation | kept chat's notices, scheduled results, timers, "Now always on" memory notices | only the temporary chat's own messages and replies |
| Layer 2 live: Mac line (time, place), models, browsers' connections, running apps | yes | yes |
| Layer 2 live: schedules, reminders, timers | yes | no |
| Layer 2 situation (now, ages) | yes | yes (ages of its own entries) |
| Layer 2 front window + screenshot | yes | no (never captured) |
| Layer 6 questions | every open question | its own tasks' only |
| System prompt: profile | no | no (not read) |
| System prompt: facts from memory (time meanings) | yes | no |
| Workers/checkers/resolver instructions: schedules, reminders | yes | no |

On Layer 1, ORCH-699 rules out "profile, memory, earlier chat or earlier tasks" and keeps "all of FERB's tools".
Journal 187 kept the `device.facts` lookup, which returns these same Mac and browser facts. So Layer 1 and the
Mac/browser lines of Layer 2 stay: they are what the tools act on, not memory. The prompts' "Remember and forget" and
"Schedules and reminders" sections are instructions only (his span's system prompt has no schedule or reminder id in
it).

**Evidence.**
- ferb-supervisor `tests/temporary_chat.rs`, 9 tests. The harness seeds:
  - a kept-chat message and reply, a notice with no conversation, a reminder delivered and a scheduled run's result;
  - schedules and reminders (`owner_state`) and a memory fact (`meanings`);
  - a screen captured at send (`capture`) and an open question of a kept task.

  What they show:
  - `a_kept_turn_reads_the_kept_chat_the_owner_state_and_the_screen` (control): the kept planner reads all of these,
    plus a screenshot, and a worker's instructions carry the schedules and reminders.
  - `a_fresh_turn_reads_no_kept_chat_owner_state_or_screen`: no planner, worker or checker call carries any of the
    14 markers or ids, every call has 0 images, and every role's instructions are read with `fresh`.
  - `a_temporary_chat_reads_its_own_earlier_turn_and_nothing_kept` (clarify_then_answer, both fresh): the second
    planner's Layer 5 conversation holds "Owner: find me a table tonight" and FERB's clarify, and nothing kept.
  - `a_temporary_conversation_holds_only_its_own_rows`: the timeline for `temporary:abc` against `s1`, and both

- Each cause was checked by reverting its fix alone; the fresh test then failed on it:
  - conversation → the notice;
  - live facts → `sc-INVENTED0001`;
  - instructions → a call's instructions carried the owner state and memory fact;

  - questions → the kept question.
