## 2026-11-24 · 219 · A phone on the wrong account can always change it: Use another account

**The owner (PHN-842).** On Android, signed in with another account than the Mac's: "in phone when ive signedin witha n
id, theres no option to change it so theres no way i can move forward cause i selected the id thats not the same as

"You're signed in as …"; Settings opens only after pairing, and pairing needs the same account (PHN-828). On Android the
signed-in line did open the account sheet when tapped, but nothing said so; the iPhone had "Use another account" there
and under the pairing refusal (journal 200), through the Sign out question, whose words ("It's unpaired from your
Mac…") don't fit a phone that isn't paired.

**What changed, both phones alike.**
- The phone-first page: "You're signed in as {email}." (now on the iPhone too; a tap still opens the account sheet with
  Sign out and Delete account…, on the iPhone too) and under it "Use another account". The pairing page under the Mac's
  refusal of this phone's account (`account_mismatch`, `mac_signed_out`, `account_unconfirmed`, the iPhone's set; Android
  now keeps the link's code as `pairErrorCode`) and the removed page when the Mac removed the phone over its account
  (Android's `removedNote`, the iPhone's `removedWords`) get "Use another account" as a grey pill.
- "Use another account" is Settings' Sign out without its question (nothing is paired on those pages, so nothing is
  lost): `FerbViewModel.signOut` / `AppModel.signOut`. Its pending state shows at once: `busy` "account" turns the link
  into FERB's running mark and "Signing out…" (the pill's words become "Signing out…") and the page's taps wait; a
  second tap says "FERB is still working on that. One moment." (PHN-656).
- The sign-out itself (PHN-843, refining PHN-841): the Mac forgotten as before (Android always; the iPhone only when
  something was paired, as before), then the site is told first (`POST /api/app/signout` with the refresh token and the
  access token while good), bounded by the requests' own timeouts (Android 15 s connect, 20 s read; iPhone 20 s), then
  the account and tokens on the phone are cleared whatever it answered. Any answer but 200 (offline, 503) leaves the
  line "You're signed out on this phone. FERB couldn't reach its sign-in to tell it, but nothing on this phone can use
  your account anymore." on the sign-in page; the next sign-in clears it. Before, the phone cleared first and told the
  site in the background, so a failure could only show later. The pairing's refusal (`pairError`, its code) and the
  removal's words now go with the account, so after signing in again the phone-first page comes, not the old refusal
  (both phones kept the refusal before: a stale line on the next pairing page).
- The sign-in page after it is the same page: Google's start sends `prompt=select_account` (site/api/_lib/deps.js:84,
  read, unchanged), so Google shows its account chooser in Android's Custom Tab and the iPhone's shared sheet. Apple on
  the web lets the person pick an Apple ID; the iPhone's system Sign in with Apple uses the phone's own Apple ID.
- `account_other` is now Android's string (strings.py no longer adds it for iOS only); the catalog is rewritten.

**Sweep for other dead ends** (phone flows where the account can't be changed before or during pairing):
- Sign-in page states: the browser closed without an answer brings the buttons back (Android `browserLeft`, the iPhone's
  sheet cancel); "finishing" is bounded by the request timeouts. No dead end.
- Phone-first page: fixed (above).
- Pairing page reached with "pair now" or for a phone paired before (wiped, removed, keys): no account shown, but a

## 2026-11-24 · 220 · The account audit's fixes: a sign-in the site ends keeps the pairing, and every failure says why

**The owner (REL-453).** An audit of the account system listed fourteen gaps; he answered "yes" to fixing all of them.
His decision supersedes nothing: REL-445 states no reuse rule, PHN-828's "a phone that signs out is unpaired" is the
person's own Sign out (unchanged), and APP-1138/PHN-841's sign-out and delete paths stand. The agent rulings are new
and extend the old ones: REL-454 (site), APP-1139 (FERB.app), PHN-844 (phones and the daemon's pairing check). Builds on
journal 219 (PHN-842, PHN-843).

**The list, item by item.**
1. *Reuse.* The site keeps only token hashes, so a rotation's pair is now derived: `successorOf(AUTH_SECRET, old
   refresh) = fa1_/fr1_ + HMAC-SHA256("ferb-app-rotate/v1.access|refresh." + old)` (app.js), issued at the rotation's own
   time. `useRefresh` (store.js): a fresh use as before; else, used under 60 s ago (`REFRESH_GRACE`), unrevoked, unexpired
   and the derived refresh token neither used nor revoked: `{replay}`, and the same pair is answered again
   (`issueTokens` is `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so a first request that died after marking the token used is finished by
   the retry); else the family is revoked as before. Clients: a refresh with no answer is sent again at once with the
   same token (Mac `rotate`, Android `access`, iPhone `refreshNow`); the Mac's 20 s request timeout stays (a longer one
   could put the retry outside the grace; Android's is 15 s connect + 20 s read, so its retry starts within 35 s).
   A sign-out by the site no longer unpairs: Android `ended` now carries the site's reason and FerbViewModel forgets the
   Mac only for `account_deleted`; iPhone `onSignedOutBySite(reason)` the same; the Mac's `account.clear` never removed
   phones. Save failures: Mac `saveUnsaved` (3 tries, then kept in memory, saved first at the next refresh/check/load,
   and `load()` prefers it over the Keychain's spent token); Android `keep` uses the new pair at once and `saveAgain`
   before the next refresh/check; iPhone `keep(fresh: false)` the same (it used to keep the old, spent token in memory
   when the Keychain refused).
2. *Expiry.* The same path: `reason: "expired"` (the row still there) asks to sign in again and keeps the pairing.
3. *Names.* Site: `keptName` (code points, control characters to spaces, 200 max, cut) for Google, both Apple paths
   (the native one no longer refuses a long name); apple.js and handlers.js cut by code points. Daemon: `checked()`
   counts characters and cuts the name to 200 instead of refusing. iPhone sends at most 200 code points.
4. *Mac words.* `AccountReply` gains `.unavailable` (5xx), `.slowDown` (429) and `rejected(reason:)`; `AccountCallback
   .failed(String)` keeps the site's word. New lines: slowDown, noEmail(provider), accountConflict(provider),
   providerFailed(provider), codeExpired, signInFailed. The site's callback now sends `provider` (the provider's own
   error or an unconfirmed token; `access_denied`/`user_cancelled_authorize` stay `cancelled`), `account_conflict`, and
   `unavailable` for a database failure.
5. *Android landing.* `appLanding` links `intent://<host>/app/callback?code&state&error#Intent;scheme=https;
   package=com.ferb.phone;end` (`androidIntent`).
6. *Why the Mac was signed out.* `AccountEnded` (deleted, expired, ended) from the reason; the account step opens with
   its words (`IntroCopy.accountEnded`), Settings → Account shows them. `phonesRemoved` no longer says "your other
   account".
7. *Delete on 401.* `deleteAccount`: a refused access token is refreshed and the delete sent once more; success only on
   the site's `deleted` or a refresh refused as `account_deleted`; otherwise "FERB needs you to sign in again…".
8. *Browser step.* A Mac start with a well-formed loopback address and state gets its errors there (303 to
   `…/callback?error=not_ready|slow_down|unavailable&state=…`), also when the site isn't set up; a phone's start keeps
   its page. A callback without a valid cookie still shows a page (no trusted address; FERB.app stops waiting when the
   cookie expires). The waiting step offers Copy link (`pendingLink`, `IntroController.copyText`).
9. *Same account.* The Mac's account step says "Use the same account on your Mac and your phone." (the phones already
   said "Use the same account as on your Mac."). The daemon's mismatch adds a Hide My Email sentence when an email is
   `@privaterelay.appleid.com`. `signin_no_email` no longer implies Hide My Email fails.
10. *Prompt sign-out elsewhere.* Before: the Mac learned at launch or its 6-hourly refresh (up to 6 h); a phone at its
    next refresh, i.e. when the 1 h access token ran out at an open. Now: FERB.app's `check()` on
    `NSApplication.didBecomeActive` and `NSWorkspace.didWake`, the phones' `check()` at each open, each at most every
    5 minutes, call `GET /api/app/me`; a 401 refreshes so the site's reason arrives. The delay is now until the device
    is next used (5 minutes at most between asks), plus the Mac's 6-hourly refresh.
11. *Cleanup.* `sweep` runs after the code grant, every refresh and the iPhone's Apple sign-in (and the callback as
    before), at most every 10 minutes per instance, 500 rows per table, and also clears `ferb_app_deleted`.
12. *Owner's list.* Columns email, name, provider(s), first sign-in, last sign-in, Mac · iPhone · Android; the line "N
    people · M signed in in the last 30 days"; CSV `email,name,providers,first_signin_at,last_signin_at,mac,ios,android`.
13. *Schema.* `ensureApp` reads `obj_description(to_regclass('ferb_app_limits')::oid, 'pg_class')`; unless it is
    `ferb app schema 2` every statement runs again (each idempotent), then `COMMENT ON TABLE ferb_app_limits …`. The live
    database (no comment) gets everything once, `ferb_app_deleted` included. The SQL file ends with the same comment.
14. *Keychain.* `Account::mac_account_read` → `Err(MacUnreadable)` when the helper fails; `AccountCheck::check_read`
    refuses it as `mac_account_unreadable` (journal and audit name) with its own words, on the link's
    `account_unconfirmed` code (the phones already treat that as "nothing changed, try again"; no wire change).

**New table.** `ferb_app_deleted (token_hash, expires_at)`: on Delete account the account's unexpired refresh-token
hashes, tied to nothing, until they would have expired, so another device hears `account_deleted`. privacy.html says so.

- *Google* ("Sign in with Google branding guidelines", developers.google.com/identity/branding-guidelines, read
  2026-11-25): the G "must be the standard color version (the standard color gradient super G logo)"; "you can't
  change the size or color"; "Stick with the Google "G" with fixed padding and size"; "Don't … use an outdated Google
  "G""; scale the button keeping its proportions; padding Android/Web 12 before the G, 10 after; iOS 16 before, 12
  after; themes Light (#FFFFFF, 1 px #747775 inside, #1F1F1F), Dark (#131314, 1 px #8E918F inside, #E3E3E3), Neutral;
  font Google Sans Medium 14/20; rectangle or pill; "buttons should be approximately the same size and have similar
  visual weight". The current asset bundle (signin-assets.zip, linked from that page) draws the 2025 gradient G: the G
  path as a mask over a conic gradient (CSS `conic-gradient`, 15 stops, turned −45° by its matrix) and six blurred
  ellipses (feGaussianBlur σ = 1 unit). So the G is that one, not the four-colour flat G of older bundles (an "outdated
  G"). Its path and every number are copied from "Theme=Dark, Show text=No, Shape=Square, Platform=Android+Web.svg"
  (checked verbatim by script) and drawn as vectors: Android a Compose Canvas (the G path, then the gradient source-in
  and the ellipses source-atop with BlurMaskFilter in pixels), the iPhone and FERB.app a SwiftUI Canvas (clip to the G,
  conic gradient, `blur(radius: 1)` in the file's units). A VectorDrawable or a static SVG/PDF asset can't express
  the blur, so neither is used; there is no bitmap. Not drawn: the file's 1-unit blur on the gradient layer itself (it
  only softens where the blue ellipses cover it and at the circle's edge, 2.6 units outside the G). Against Google's own
  PNG (iOS @4x, dark, square: the G 80 px on #131314), on the G's square: Android's render mean |Δ| 1.4/255, 95th
  percentile 11, 0.02 % of pixels over 32 (all at the edge); the Swift render 1.9/255, 14, 1.2 % (edge).
  Proportions: Google's iOS button, the one nearest FERB's 52-high pill (G 20 of 44, 16 from the edge, 12 to the
  words; its words 14 of 44 are FERB's 16 of 52 within half a point). Colours: on a light surface (the phones' white
  card) Google's Dark theme exactly, for both buttons, so FERB's #000 pill becomes #131314 with the #8E918F line and
  #E3E3E3 words; on a dark surface (FERB.app's notch, the phones' FERB surface where `Pill` turns white) Google's Light

  says nothing on a full-width button's alignment; the owner's brief keeps the words centred).
- *Apple* (Human Interface Guidelines, Sign in with Apple, read from developer.apple.com's JSON 2026-11-25; change log
  last 2022-09-14): custom buttons may "align logos across multiple sign-in buttons" and "adjust the button's font,

## 2026-11-25 · 222 · The phone shows the owner's relay in every phase, and falls back only after 30 s it watched

**The owner.** On his Android phone, with his own relay set on the Mac: the Mac page showed "Connecting…", the note
"Your relay can't be reached; the public relay is used until it is back." and, in the card, "Your own relay — Not
set"; a few seconds later it corrected itself. "Not set" was false: the phone knows the relay from pairing and earlier
welcomes.

**"Not set": the cause.** `LinkStatus.own_relay_url` (ferb-mobile-ffi `link.rs`) is read from the link's current
phase, and ferb-link's client put `own_relay` only in the online phase, copied from the welcome. In `connecting`,
`waiting`, `stopped`, `paused` it was absent, so both apps (Android `Main.kt` `Mac`, the iPhone's `Tabs.swift`
`MacPage`, and each one's own-relay sheet, all reading `ownRelayUrl`) showed "Not set" whenever the phone wasn't
online, which is also when the fallback note shows. The relay itself was never forgotten: it is saved in the phone's
state (`MacTarget.own`, from the pairing code, replaced by each welcome or pushed relay change in `learn_relay`) and the
dial used it throughout.

**"Not set": the fix.** One shared path in ferb-link's client: `Phone::phase()` and every `state` event carry
`own_relay`, the saved relay's address (null with none set, or once the pairing is forgotten), in every phase; the
online phase no longer copies it from the welcome (`learn_relay` saved the same value just before). ferb-mobile-ffi
reads it as before, so both apps show the owner's relay while connecting, offline, stopped or on the public relay
without any app change; the iPhone takes the same `LinkStatus.ownRelayUrl`. ferb-mobile's core ignores the field. The
Mac's `link.status` `own_relay` is the bridge's own and is unchanged.

**The fallback note while "Connecting…": the cause.** The note is the phone's own relay policy state (`relay_state`
events, kept by ferb-mobile-ffi until the next one), independent of the link's phase. `RelayPolicy::run` (ferb-link
`net.rs`) checks every 500 ms and falls back after `own_relay_fallback_after_s` (30) of the own relay not being a
connected home relay; once fallen back it stays until a probe answers, every `own_relay_probe_s` (60). Two flaws, the
first very likely what the owner saw (the phone opened after being frozen in the background, on a change to mobile
data; inferred, no phone log read): `down_since` was wall time from the first check that saw the relay down, so a
process frozen right after such a check fell back on the first check after it woke, counting the frozen minutes as
unreachability; and a change of network or the app coming back to the front did nothing to the policy, so a fallback
taken on the old network (or while frozen) lasted until the next 60 s probe, and an unreachability window begun on the
old network carried over to the new one. PHN-208/PHN-425 mean 30 s of observed unreachability, so both are bugs under
them (the coordinator's ruling: method ours, no owner question).

**The fallback: the fix.** In `net.rs`, `DownWindow` counts only watched time: a gap between two checks longer than
`WATCH_GAP` (5 s, ten ticks) starts the window again instead of counting toward it. `RelayPolicy::recheck()` makes the
next check (within 500 ms) probe the own relay at once when in `own_fallback`, and otherwise start the window afresh.
The phone calls it from `network_changed_to` and from `set_active(true)`, which both apps call on a change of network
and on coming to the front (Android `AndroidSignals.kt`, the iPhone's `Signals.swift`). The Mac runs the same policy, so
its window also ignores time it slept; nothing on the Mac calls `recheck`. No limit changed.

**Evidence.** Checks by each crate's own manifest as `engine/gate.sh` runs them, in a worktree, through
`ferb-test-guard` (build folder reached by a short link: the stand-in daemon's Unix socket path in
`CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` passes macOS's 104-byte limit under the long worktree path): `cargo fmt --check` for the three
phone crates; `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` for ferb-link (`--features devrelay`) and ferb-mobile-ffi;
`cargo test`: ferb-link 76 passed, 5 ignored, 0 failed (19 binaries); ferb-mobile-ffi 23 passed; ferb-mobile 109
passed.
- ferb-mobile-ffi `tests/link.rs` `the_status_carries_the_saved_own_relay_while_the_mac_cant_be_reached` (new): a
  paired phone saved with an own relay, its Mac unreachable on 127.0.0.1: the status in `connecting` and `waiting`,
  and every status the app heard, carries the relay; after Forget it is none. Against HEAD's `client.rs` it fails with
  the owner's status exactly (`phase: Connecting, paired: true, own_relay_url: None`).
- ferb-link `tests/relay.rs` `own_relay_down_falls_back_to_the_shared_relay_and_comes_back` (extended): every
  `connecting`/`waiting` state event during the outage, and the phase on the public relay, carry the owner's relay.
- ferb-link `net.rs` `only_watched_time_counts_toward_the_fallback` (new, unit): 30 s of 500 ms checks reach 30 s; a
  check, ten frozen minutes, then a check: 0 s, and 30 s more of checks are needed; a gap of `WATCH_GAP` counts, one
  past it restarts; `clear` restarts.
- ferb-link `tests/relay.rs` `a_network_change_or_the_app_in_front_probes_the_own_relay_at_once` (new): the own relay
  down, the phone falls back (3 s window), the relay comes back, with `own_relay_probe_s` 600 the phone stays on the
  fallback for 3 s without a nudge; then `network_changed_to("cellular")` (first round) or `set_active(true)` (second
  round) brings it off the fallback in 5.5 s both times and back on its relay. (Most of the 5.5 s is inferred to
  be the probe itself on the test relays' plain HTTP, not measured step by step.) Not run against the code before the
  change: without `recheck` the 600 s probe can't come within the test's 10 s.
Android `:app:testDebugUnitTest` (`--offline --no-daemon`, host library rebuilt from this change): 374 tests, 0
failures. (A first run, before the policy part, had 1 failure:
`AccountFlowTest.the_macs_refusal_of_this_account_offers_another_account_and_signing_out_clears_it`, line 465, against
FakePhone, which this change doesn't touch; the class alone then passed 19/19, and this full run passed it. I infer a
timing flake, not proved.) The iPhone has no
change (it reads the same field and calls the same `setActive`/`networkChanged`), so `apps/ios/tools/build.sh test`
didn't run. `tools/kb/run kb check`: ok; no kb change (no ruling of the owner's changed).

**Unverified.** No device, no install, no live check: the owner's own-relay pages while connecting and on the fallback
are not seen on a real phone, nor a real freeze and thaw (the frozen gap is tested on the window alone, with made-up
instants; the loop's use of it is read, not run frozen). The 3:40 sequence is inferred from the code, not from the
phone's log. A probe made at the very moment of a network change can fail if the new network isn't usable yet; the
next one is then the regular `own_relay_probe_s` later (or the next change or opening).

## 2026-11-25 · 223 · "Stop using my relay" asks first

At 3:45 the owner pressed "Stop using my relay" in Settings → Phone by mistake (journal `phone.relay_set {"on": false}`,
the only caller FERB.app's PhonePage button); the Mac keeps no copy of a removed relay link, so the phone then showed
"Not set" correctly. The link was read back from his relay server (`/opt/ferb-relay`, over his own SSH shortcut,
straight into his clipboard, never shown). He said yes to asking first (APP-1142): the button is "Stop using my
relay…" and opens an alert, "Stop using your relay?", "Your phones move to the public relay. FERB doesn't keep the
relay's link, so to use it again you'll need the link from your server.", with Stop Using It (destructive) and Cancel.
PhoneSettingsTests pass; the alert itself is the owner's to see (untestable reason recorded).

## 2026-11-25 · 226 · Claude Code's own end breakpoint is cached for five minutes; FERB's marker keeps the hour

**What Claude Code does (T-1324).** Read from the pinned Claude Code 2.1.310's bundled code (the darwin-arm64 binary
FERB.app carries, its strings only; nothing was run, no sign-in, no network). Each request it sends gets breakpoints on
its system blocks (TTL `KR`) and on its message markers, the last block of the newest message(s) (TTL `NE`, in its
`ykr`/`F_r`: a marked user message's last block gets `cache_control` with that TTL, replacing one already there;
FERB's marker on an earlier block is kept as sent). Both TTLs come from one choice (`Mve`): `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M`,
else `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL` for its main-thread sources (`sdk` among them; FERB sets "1h"), else settings, else
the hour for a subscriber. Only `NE` has its own switch: `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGES_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL`, an enum taking only
"5m" (`jZ`): then the message markers go without a TTL (five minutes) while the system ones and the
`extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11` beta stay. `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING` turns off every marker of its own and that beta,
and there is no switch to leave the message markers off alone. So a planner turn (one user message: FERB's stable
prefix with its 1-hour marker, then the live facts and the new message) wrote everything after FERB's marker at the
hour, and the next turn, whose tail differs, read only up to FERB's marker: journal 208's measurement.

**Fix (RUN-476, Claude adapter only).** A run whose request has text after FERB's marker (`tail_after_marker`: the
blocks FERB sends, blank text dropped as Claude Code drops it) starts Claude Code with
`CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGES_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=5m`. When FERB's marked block ends the request, Claude Code's marker lands on
that same block and would turn FERB's hour into five minutes, so the setting is left off there (today's behaviour, as
RUN-437 does for the API loop). This is RUN-436's shape (the owner's: instructions and history at the hour, the tail at
five minutes) on Claude Code too, for planners and workers alike: a run's later calls are seconds apart and read the
tail within five minutes.

**Expected cost.** Anthropic's prices: a 5-minute write is 1.25x input, a 1-hour write 2x, a read 0.1x (0.05x on Opus
5.5). A kept chat's tail (8.7k-10k tokens a turn) goes from 17.4k-20k input-token equivalents to 10.9k-12.5k, about
6.5k-7.5k saved a turn (37.5% of that write); a temporary chat's (5.6k-6.8k) saves 4.2k-5.1k. On Opus 5.5 ($4 input,
$5 and $8 per MTok for the two writes) about 3 cents a kept-chat turn at API prices; on the owner's subscription it is
usage counted toward his limits. Reads of FERB's prefix are unchanged. The one case that can cost more: a gap over five
minutes between two calls of one run (a tool call that waits that long) rewrites the tail at 1.25x instead of reading
it, as the API loop already does under RUN-436.

**Live check (LIVE-1216, the owner runs it).** Three messages a minute or two apart in one chat with Claude as the
planner, then one in a temporary chat; each planner run's usage (`ferb trace TASK --json`, the model span: Claude
Code's result usage carries `cache_creation` by TTL, read by usage.rs `from_anthropic`): `cache_write_1h_tokens` only the
new stable part (a few hundred tokens or 0), `cache_write_5m_tokens` the tail (what journal 208 saw written at the
hour), `cached_input_tokens` on the later turns still FERB's prefix (about 52k-54k in a kept chat).

**Evidence.** ferb-runtimes: `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt` clean, every test binary ok
(claude 3: claude_matches_python with RUN-476's named difference on every recorded case's Claude Code spawn, new
claude_code_starts_with_its_message_breakpoints_at_five_minutes_unless_ferbs_marker_ends_the_request and
claude_codes_end_breakpoint_is_five_minutes_only_where_a_tail_follows_ferbs_marker; api, claude_long_lines, codex,
codex_cache, compact, mcp, real_process, tables, unit). `kb check` ok after `kb lock` and `kb gen`. T-1324 closed;
ORCH-325 is linked to LIVE-1216 now that its last open task is gone.

**Unverified.** Nothing ran against Claude Code or the API: that 2.1.310 reads the setting as its code says, that the
API then reports the tail under `ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`, and the saving itself wait on LIVE-1216. I inferred that
FERB's runs use the `sdk` query source; the change doesn't depend on it (the switch applies to every source). How
often a worker's calls are more than five minutes apart was not measured. The whole workspace gate was not run (the
ferb-runtimes crate only).
